claim: At the bump station x/L = -0.4 the fine-grid learned wall is closer in skin friction and farther in mean velocity over the 120 common measured heights (mean absolute discrepancy 0.010 against 0.016 of freestream speed). The source states the same: the equilibrium model "outperforms the RLWMs in velocity prediction, even though its prediction of mean skin friction is less ideal". The difference arises below y/L of about 0.016, where the learned profile lies about 0.05 above the measurements. Above y/L = 0.02 both profiles lie above the measurements by about 0.011 and 0.007, and a measured profile higher by 0.009 would reverse that order. Statistics span 1.5 flow-through times. Crest friction is closer for the learned wall. At the ten recovery taps both models miss by 0.07 to 0.33 in Cp (means 0.20 and 0.24) and the learned wall is farther at each by 0.02 to 0.05; the source calls these differences minor. At Re_H = 37,000 on the hill the source states that the equilibrium simulations "match or even surpass" the learned ones in velocity "despite their inaccurate predictions of C_f".
